My parents left me, my sister, and my brother alone in the house. My sister is 18, I'm 17, and my brother is 12. My parents made my sister "in charge" while they were away. I guess that means she's supposed to take care of us and make sure everything is okay. On Sunday, I wanted to go out with my girlfriend for dinner. My sister told me I couldn't leave. When I asked why, she said, "Because I said so." At first, I thought she was joking, so I laughed. But she wasn't joking, and she kept insisting I couldn't go. I told her she can boss around my little brother but not me, and I went out with my girlfriend anyway. When I came home, my younger brother had told my mom about the "fight" we had. My mom called me and said I'm grounded and have to do whatever my sister says because she's "in charge." I tried to protest, but my mom wasn't having it, and I ended up being grounded for disobeying my sister who's acting like a pseudo-parent while they're away. I dropped it because I don't think it's worth arguing with my mom. Plus, my brother told me afterward that he was the one who told mom, and I forgave him because I can't be mad at that little turd for too long. So, the question is: Did I do the right thing? Is it AITA (Ask if I'm the Asshole) here? First, I need to think about the roles and responsibilities in this situation. My sister is 18, and my parents left her in charge. That means she's supposed to take care of the household and make sure everyone follows the rules. I'm 17, and while I'm almost an adult, I'm still technically a minor, and my parents have given my sister the authority to manage things while they're away. When my sister told me I couldn't go out with my girlfriend, she was exercising the authority my parents gave her. I, on the other hand, decided to ignore her and go out anyway. That's where the conflict arises. By not respecting her authority, I'm essentially challenging the structure my parents set up. But then, I also have to consider the dynamics between me and my sister. It seems like she has an easier time making my little brother obey her but struggles with me. That might indicate that our relationship is a bit tense, and there's some underlying conflict that's not being addressed. When I came home and found out I was grounded, I tried to protest but ultimately dropped it. That shows that I recognize my mom's authority and don't want to escalate the situation further. However, I also forgave my brother for tattling on me, which is a mature response. So, is it AITA? Did I act like an asshole in this situation? Well, I went against my sister's instructions, which were given to me by my parents. That's a clear disregard for the rules set by my parents. However, I also have the right to make my own decisions, especially as I'm approaching adulthood. But in this case, my parents have explicitly put my sister in charge, so I should respect that. On the other hand, my sister might have overstepped by trying to control me in a way that's not reasonable. Maybe she's taking her role too seriously and using it to exert power over me unnecessarily. I also need to consider the impact of my actions on the family dynamic. By challenging my sister's authority, I might be creating tension that affects everyone in the house. It's important to maintain a harmonious environment, especially when parents are away. In the end, I think I did make a mistake by not respecting my sister's authority as designated by my parents. However, I also think there's room for communication and setting boundaries to ensure that everyone's needs and feelings are respected. Maybe the best approach would be to talk to my sister calmly and explain how I feel about her controlling my actions. At the same time, I should acknowledge that she's in charge and that I need to respect her role. Finding a balance between asserting my independence and respecting the hierarchy set by my parents is key. Overall, while I might have acted impulsively by going out without respecting my sister's instructions, I also have the right to express my feelings and seek a healthier dynamic within the family. It's a tricky situation, and there's no clear right or wrong, but working towards open communication and mutual respect can help resolve the conflict.
